n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.1: What is a GPU, and why does memory matter?
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.2: Language models run on GPUs. A GPU has thousands of small calculators working at the same time, and its own fast memory. To follow the rest of the module, one image is enough: a kitchen with a great many cooks, but a rather narrow door to the pantry.
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.3: The cooks are the compute. A modern datacenter card like the H100 does around a thousand trillion multiplications per second.
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.4: The pantry is the GPU memory (VRAM), for example 80 GB. The model's weights and the KV cache live there.
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.5: The door is the memory bandwidth, about 3.35 TB per second. Every ingredient the cooks use has to be carried in through it.
n6b.vad-ar-ett-grafikkort.6: When the model writes a word, all 16 GB of weights must be carried in through the door, but the cooks do only a little work with them. Mostly they stand and wait. That is what memory-bound means, and it explains almost everything in the rest of the course: why you write for many users at once, why the KV cache matters so much and why it pays to quantize.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.2: Imagine writing an essay and having to reread the whole text from the start before every new word. It gets slower with every word. The KV cache is the model's notes: it saves what is needed from every earlier word, so that only the new word has to be processed.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.3: What is storedFor every earlier word, its key (the label) and value (the content) from attention are stored, on every floor. Hence the name: K and V.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.4: How it is usedWhen a new word is to be written, only its own key, value and query are computed. The query is compared with all stored keys, and the stored values are mixed.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.5: ResultThe same answer as without a cache, but the work per word is constant instead of growing with the length of the text.
n6b.kv-cache-i-klartext.6: The priceThe notes take memory: in Llama-3-8B about 128 KB per word. So a conversation of 8,000 words takes roughly 1 GB of GPU memory for as long as it runs.
